title: post-upgrade-quickfire-smoke-and-terraform-checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practitioner-friendly post-upgrade smoke and quick-troubleshoot checklist for VPC/on-prem deployments. It's intentionally terse so on-call or SRE can run through in 10–25 minutes after a control-plane or runtime upgrade. Mix of Terraform sanity checks, runtime smoke hits, and common failure fingerprints with immediate mitigations.

Notes on scope and tone:
- Focus: failures seen during installs and upgrades (model load failures, kernel mismatch, container runtime changes, network/firewall, KMS failures, TF state drift).
- This is a working doc — add commands, observations, or new fingerprints you encounter.
- If you identify a new recurring pattern, add a short blurb under "Known failure fingerprints" and attach a log snippet.

Quick summary checklist (run in parallel where possible):
1) Control plane health 
   - Confirm control plane components (api, auth, config) are green in console. If console is unreachable, try direct pod checks.
   - kubectl -n redwood get po -l app=control-plane
   - Expected: all pods Ready=1/1 or Ready=2/2, restarts minimal.

2) Terraform sanity (before/after upgrade)
   - cd infra/terraform/private && terraform init -upgrade
   - terraform validate && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan.postupgrade
   - Inspect plan for unexpected resource replacements. If plan wants to replace >1 node pool or >1 network resource, pause.

3) Node and GPU health
   - ssh to a sample node (or use SSM) and run:
     - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,mig.mode.current --format=csv
     - systemctl status docker|containerd
     - dmesg | tail -n 80 (look for NVML/cuda errors, kernel OOM killers)

4) Basic runtime endpoint smoke hits (local agent)
   - curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/health | jq .
     - Expect {"status":"ok"} within 2s.
   - curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwkv-small","input":"hello","max_tokens":8}' | jq .
     - Expect a short text completion and no 5xx.
   - Run embeddings quick check: curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-compact","input":"test"}'

5) Latency & resource sanity
   - top / htop to verify no runaway process (runtime consuming 100% CPU).
   - nvidia-smi to see GPU memory use — abnormal if all GPUs saturated by init processes.
   - pod-level: kubectl -n redwood top pod <runtime-pod> --containers

6) Logs to inspect (fast greps)
   - runtime logs: kubectl -n redwood logs <runtime-pod> --tail=500 | egrep -i "error|fail|exception|OOM|cuda|nvml|mmap|permission|kms|hsm"
   - model load failures often show: "failed to load model: mmap: invalid argument" or "quantize: unsupported bitwidth"
   - KMS/HSM: look for 403/timeout to key-endpoint or "unable to decrypt key blob"

7) Networking checks (VPC-specific)
   - From a node: curl -v https://control-plane.internal:443 (TLS handshake success)
   - iptables -L -n | egrep "443|8080|22|10250" — ensure no DENY rules for required ports.
   - DNS: dig control-plane.internal @127.0.0.1 +short (should resolve to cluster IP).

8) Health of backing services
   - S3-compatible store: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-model-artifacts --endpoint-url https://minio.internal || check minio logs
   - Redis: redis-cli -h redis.internal ping (PONG expected)

Immediate mitigations (1–10 minutes)
- If control-plane pods CrashLoopBackOff after upgrade: roll back control-plane deployment to previous image tag (kubectl set image ...). If image unavailable, scale down new replicas and scale previous ReplicaSet back up.
- If terraform plan indicates an accidental resource replacement (network or NAT): pause the upgrade, open a ticket, and revert any apply that started.
- GPU driver/kernel mismatch: revert to previous driver or reboot nodes into the pre-upgrade kernel (documented in node-provision playbook). If rebooting, cordon and drain with graceful timeout (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
- Model load OOMs: reduce concurrency for that runtime node pool (autoscaler target) or restart runtime with environment variable REDWOOD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 temporarily.
- KMS/HSM access failures: revert to local key cache or fallback key policy if available; if not, escalate to Security on-call.

Known failure fingerprints and quick tips (add bullets as you encounter new ones)
- mmap/permission denied on model load:
  - Cause: selinux or restrictive mount flags on the artifact volume OR model file mode bits wrong after a copy.
  - Fingerprint: "mmap: permission denied" or "operation not permitted" in runtime logs.
  - Mitigation: chmod 644 model files, verify mount options (nosuid,nodev noexec?). Remount with exec if needed.

- NVML unreachable / driver mismatch:
  - Fingerprint: "NVML: Driver not loaded" or nvmlSt_unsupported_version
  - Mitigation: check kernel module (lsmod | grep nvidia), reinstall driver via gpu-driver role, reboot if module can't be reloaded.

- Quantization/Kernel mismatch errors after model-compiler changes:
  - Fingerprint: "unsupported kernel" or "quantize: kernel symbol missing"
  - Mitigation: fallback to pre-compiled model artifact or re-run compile job. If immediate serving needed, point route to a compatible model variant.

- Container runtime change (dockerd -> containerd) caused init hangs:
  - Fingerprint: pod stuck in ContainerCreating with events showing "failed to start containerd-shim"
  - Mitigation: ensure CRI socket path in kubelet config and restart kubelet. Verify runtimeClass entries.

Terraform module quick-notes (things we've tripped on)
- State drift: If terraform state was partially applied (manual changes on nodes), use terraform state rm/import carefully. Always make a plan with -out and review replacements.
- Provider version pinning: upgrades of the cloud provider plugin have led to renamed fields causing replacement of network attachments. Keep a small matrix of allowed provider versions for each environment.
- TF module quirks: module.redwood.vpc submodule changes historically replaced route tables when cidr was normalized. When upgrading module, explicitly set lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["route_table"] } if you're uncertain.
- Resource locking: our remote state lock sometimes fails under network flakiness — abort and retry; never force-unlock unless you know the operator who left a session.

Post-upgrade gating (what must be green before marking done)
- Control plane API: /health OK from at least 3 distinct AZs (or nodes)
- 95th pct latency for sample generation < 2x previous baseline (run auto-bench script)
- Model artifact download/checksum validation success for top 5 models (curl artifact URLs and sha256sum)
- No new CrashLoopBackOff events in last 30 minutes across runtime namespace

Rollback plan (fast-path)
1) Pause triggering CI/CD pipeline / disable upgrade gate.
2) Re-deploy previous control-plane image tag (kubectl set image deployment/control-plane control-plane=redwood/control-plane:<previous>) and scale to known replica count.
3) If nodes were replaced: run terraform apply with previous module versions (apply from saved plan if available).
4) Repoint traffic: adjust routing policy to route 100% traffic to the previous capacity pool.
5) Post-rollback: run sanity smoke tests above and open a postmortem ticket with logs and plan diff.

Escalation matrix (who to call when)
- Infra SRE (first): Diego Alvarez
- Runtime/Serving lead: Priya Nair
- Security/KMS: John Rivera
- Platform Eng (terraform/kernel): Alex Morgan
- Pager channel: #infra-private-deploy (use ~/ops/pager-rotation to check on-call)

Short checklist to paste in an incident channel:
- "Ran post-upgrade quick smoke: control-plane OK, runtime health checks failed with model load OOM on 2/3 runtime pods. Temporarily set REDWOOD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 on affected pool and rolling restart. Terraform plan showed no destructive changes. Investigating driver kernel mismatch. Notified SRE (Diego) and Runtime (Priya)."

Open questions / TODOs (add notes here)
- Add a quick script that runs all three smoke HTTP hits and returns a single JSON summary (health, generate, embeddings) with timings.
- Maintain a short mapping of model variants -> compatible runtime binary version for faster rollback routing.
- Capture a set of 5 canonical model artifact checksums per environment to avoid accidental corrupt uploads.

Appendix: quick commands reference
- Terraform: terraform init -upgrade; terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan.tf; terraform apply "plan.tf"
- Kube: kubectl -n redwood get po -o wide; kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --tail=200; kubectl -n redwood exec -it <pod> -- sh -c 'ps aux | egrep "runtime|model"'
- Node: ssh ubuntu@node-1 sudo journalctl -u runtime -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80

Historical notes (why this doc exists)
- Compiled after three incidents in 2025 where driver upgrades + terraform module bump coincided, causing model load failures and a 45-minute outage window. The goal is to reduce triage time and provide deterministic mitigations.

---
If you edit this doc: please add the minimal reproduction or a log snippet for any new fingerprint. Keep items short and actionable.
